title: Two Joints and a Plunger: The SCARA, Its Closed Form Reach, Its Two Elbows, and Why Its Joints Carry No Weight

questions.question: Why are a SCARA's first two joints cheap to hold up?
options: Their axes are vertical, so gravity puts no torque on them
Their links are short, so the lever of the load is small
A spring in each joint balances the weight
The slide carries half the load and they share the rest
questions.explanation: Gravity acts along a vertical axis and so has no lever about it. A 2 kg payload put 0.0 N m on those joints, against 7.85 N m on the shoulder of a six axis arm holding it 0.4 m out.

questions.question: How many elbow solutions has a point within reach?
options: One, since the slide fixes the height
Four: two elbows for each direction of the roll
Two, plus or minus the arccosine
As many as there are headings of the tool
questions.explanation: It is the two link problem in a plane: the cosine of the second joint is fixed by the distance, and the angle is plus or minus its arccosine. Left elbow and right.

questions.question: The determinant when straight was:
options: 0.2250, the length of a link
questions.explanation: The determinant is l1 l2 times the sine of the second joint, which is zero when the arm is straight and when it is folded. It was 0.0506 at a right angle.

questions.question: A point 0.5 m out for these links was:
options: Reached with the arm straight
Refused
Reached with the left elbow only
Reached by using the slide
questions.explanation: Two links of 0.225 m reach 0.45 m at most. The function says so and does not return the nearest point.

questions.question: What task suits a SCARA?
options: Welding along a tilted seam
Reaching into a box from the side
Carrying a heavy part between two heights
Pick and place on a flat table, from above
questions.explanation: It moves fast in a plane, is stiff vertically and cannot tilt. That is a part picked from above and put down flat.

questions.question: What does a SCARA not do?
options: Turn its tool about the vertical
Move its tool up and down
Tilt its tool
Reach the same point with either elbow
questions.explanation: Its four joints give x, y, height and a roll about the vertical. There is nothing to tip the tool away from straight down.
